title: Post-incident follow-up: KV-cache shadow routing + A/B telemetry mismatch
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: During an A/B experiment that introduced model v2 behind a canary + shadow configuration, we observed a subtle regression in output quality and a P95 latency increase for shadowed requests. Shadow traffic routing interacted with the KV cache key namespace in the runtime and caused rare key collisions that changed cache hit rates for the canary cohort. The automated rollback did not trigger because the telemetry pipeline aggregated metrics differently for shadow vs active cohorts, masking the median shift and preventing the computed rollback condition from firing.

This ticket tracks the incident follow-ups: concrete runbook updates, telemetry contract fixes, integration tests to reproduce the KV keyspace collision, and a safety harness to validate auto-rollback triggers in future experiments.
comments: Priya Nair (2025-11-04): Initial incident log attached to the confluence doc. Key symptoms: +7% P95 latency for A/B cohort, +3% generation divergence on golden prompt suite, KV cache hit-rate drop from 82% to 46% for the canary nodes.

Diego Martinez (2025-11-06): Reproduced locally with a synthetic shadow driver. Found that the shadow router used a hashing salt that overlapped with canary keys when request context included user-scoped prefixes.
Ava Chen (2025-11-09): Observability gap confirmed: shadow telemetry uses sampling path that aggregates across routes by default; need a per-cohort telemetry tag to avoid aggregation blind spots.

Liam O'Connor (2025-11-11): Suggested changes to rollout controller to require both central tendency and tail signals before suppressing an auto-rollback; otherwise fallback to safe-variant immediately.
Priya Nair (2025-11-15): Drafted runbook edits and posted link to PRs for runtime and rollout-controller. Planning synthetic test in CI to run before any canary that enables shadowing.
actions: Runbook: Add a pre-rollout checklist entry - 'KV cache namespace collision check' with links to diagnostic commands and expected ranges.
Telemetry contract: Add explicit cohort tags (canary/shadow/active) to every metric emitted by the router and runtime; update ingestion pipeline to preserve cohort-level aggregates.
Runtime change: Introduce a per-deployment salt for KV cache keys to avoid cross-deployment collisions; default to deterministic salt derived from deployment id.
Rollout controller: Modify rollback trigger logic to evaluate both median and p95 of latency and quality metrics, and to use cohort tags when computing deltas.
Integration tests: Add a synthetic shadow harness in CI that simulates 1M requests with mixed prefixes to assert cache hit-rate invariants and canary quality thresholds; fail build on regressions.
Canary policy: Introduce a short pre-canary dry-run mode that sends small amount of synthetic production-like requests to verify cache behavior before live traffic split.
Dashboards & Alerts: New per-cohort dashboard with KV cache hit-rate, median latency, p95 latency, and golden-prompt divergence. Pager alerts if thresholds exceeded for 10m.
Postmortem: Publish detailed timeline and add a follow-up retro session with Platform and Serving teams to review long-term mitigations.
resolution:
In progress - priority fixes split across three PRs (runtime salt, telemetry tags, rollout controller). Short-term mitigations (cohort tagging and alerting) are complete; runtime salt and CI harness targeted for runtime-1.21 release.

Owner notes: After the runtime salt PR merges, we will run the synthetic harness in a staging canary that mirrors the production traffic mix and validate that the auto-rollback conditions trigger correctly in the injected-failure CI job.
postmortem_takeaways: Telemetry is the single source of truth for auto-rollback decisions; cohort-level fidelity is essential when using shadow traffic.
Caching layers that index on request context must have explicit salt boundaries per deployment to prevent accidental interference.
Auto-rollback heuristics must consider both central tendency (median) and tail behavior (p95/p99) and require cohort-tagged data for comparisons.
Synthetic shadow tests that mimic production header prefixes should run as a gate before any experiment that enables shadowing across deployments.
